Whistleblower videos reveal helicopter spraying workers with weed killers

This is the most bullshit article I've read in long long time. It contains literally one single useful word in the entire article. So the chemical they are spraying is called Velossa. That's it. This is the only useful bit in the entire piece. The rest is just fluff and I'm sorry if you had to endure it.

  • What is the intended purpose of this chemical? - No answer. (Turns out it is a broad leaf weed killer)

  • Why were they spraying that particular area? - No answer.

  • What ere they trying to achieve by spraying weed killer on the trees? - Kill the weeds or kill the trees? No answer.

  • Why was the forest worker in that area during the spraying? - No answer. Possibly his own incompetence.

  • Is this chemical dangerous? - Only scaremongering so far. Here is the MSDS Sheet of the said chemical I had to dig up because the journalist (blogger) was lazy. Not absorbed trough skin, causes irritation if inhaled. (Compare to a household cleaner MSDS Sheet)

  • What are the long term effects of this chemical to the trees and to the soil? - No answer.

In the end this seems like, 

10% - Failure to properly coordinate a spraying operation.
90% - Hot gas.

Also here are the journalistic opportunities missed by that numskull:

  • The MSDS Sheets for herbicides seem intentionally vague. Why is that? What are they trying to hide? Why is a poorly tested chemical even allowed on the market?

  • Is the forestry company trying to kill more trees than they are allowed to cut?

  • Will this substance prevent the growth of new trees in the coming years turning the forest into a desert?

Incompetent journalism and half-assed scaremongering ruined what could have been a good story.

I don't necessarily agree with a lot of Tom Sowell's conclusions, he is a fantastic writer.

In this article, Wall Street Journal is asserting that a basic well-studied law of economics is wrong. Specifically, the idea that businesses would try to cut costs does not apply.

Everyone has heard the claim that a high-wage country like the U.S. loses jobs to low-wage countries when there is free trade.

Yes, we have heard that because it is true. Actual economic theory: a business will choose lower cost inputs to maximize profits, other things equal. WSJ is actually denying this. Not very good Economics Thomas Sowell and WSJ. :D

In reality, the number of jobs in the U.S. increased by millions after NAFTA went into effect and the unemployment rate fell to low levels not seen in years.

So the "great sucking sound" of companies leaving the US didn't happen? Was the news wrong as it reported company after company leaving the US to go to lower-wage countries? Was that whole story of bypassing Mexico and going straight to China wrong? Was the increasing goods trade deficit and the national trade debt a figment of our imaginations? Did we not see massive increases in ports, including ports that brought goods into Mexico from China to trade in the new NAFTA? None of that happened because we have more jobs now?

How do the few years of computer revolution, population increase, and everything else economic fit into the equation? Or, more basically, is WSJ saying that correlation equals causation while they complain about "fallacies"?

Well, that's just the beginning of the article, and I've pointed out enough. Analyzing the rest of it would take too long.
